item.title: USS Abraham Lincoln returns to San Diego after historic 10-month deployment
item.description: The USS Abraham Lincoln docked at its homeport in the San Diego Bay on Thursday after its deployment to the Middle East nearly one year ago. CBS News' Eleanor Watson and Carter Evans report. Then, Ret. Navy Vice Adm. Robert Murrett joins with analysis.

item.title: Curtis Flowers, wrongfully convicted man who was on death row, dies at 56
item.description: One of Curtis Flowers' attorneys called his case "unprecedented in the history of the American legal system."

item.title: Trump promises not to resume Iran strikes before midterm elections
item.description: Crude oil prices had shot up on Thursday after reports President Trump was considering more strikes. They immediately dropped again after his new announcement.

item.title: Hurricane Isaias threatens Gulf Coast with rain, flooding. See its path.
item.description: Hurricane Isaias, the first Atlantic hurricane of 2026, is taking aim at the Gulf Coast from Mississippi to the Florida Panhandle.

item.title: Astonishing video shows moments after 6-year-old shot a Virginia teacher
item.description: Newly released video shows the moments after a 6-year-old boy shot a teacher in Virginia. CBS News' Shanelle Kaul reports.

item.title: Marco Rubio slams press after getting question about Kimberly Guilfoyle allegations
item.description: Secretary of State Marco Rubio reacted strongly to reporters' questions about allegations against Kimberly Guilfoyle, the U.S. ambassador to Greece.

item.title: Space station crew returns to Earth with perfect splashdown
item.description: The Crew 13 fliers completed a mission spanning more than 100 million miles with a pinpoint splashdown off the coast of Southern California.

item.title: NASA SpaceX Crew-12 returns to Earth after 8 months in space
item.description: The NASA SpaceX Crew-12 splashed down to Earth on Thursday after spending 8 months at the International Space Station. CBS News' Bill Hardwood has more.

item.title: They've been waiting since July for FEMA relief. Trump finally approved it.
item.description: Dr. Jon LaPook visited Manasha, Wisconsin, to meet residents who had been waiting for FEMA relief since July. On Wednesday night, President Trump approved nearly $18 million in relief.

item.title: Christa Pike has pneumonia, unable to move arms after botched execution
item.description: Attorneys for Christa Pike, the Tennessee inmate who survived two doses of a lethal injection during her botched execution last week, shared an update on her health condition.

item.title: FlyDubai co-pilot bashed women in thousands of "manosphere" X posts
item.description: Social media posts show the FlyDubai co-pilot accused of a hijack attempt spent a year bashing women with "manosphere" rhetoric.

item.title: Trump announces tornado aid for Menasha after CBS News report
item.description: President Trump announced nearly $18 million in federal disaster aid for Wisconsin one day after CBS News reported on residents still waiting for aid following a devastating tornado.

item.title: Judge presses Justice Department on justifications for White House media ban
item.description: Lawyers for CNN, MS NOW and Politico were back in court as the legal battle continues over President Trump's decision to ban their reporters from the White House.

item.title: Russian guided missile kills 30 on packed Ukrainian city buses
item.description: Russian missiles have hit an apartment building and civilian buses, killing more than 50 people in two days, as the Kremlin says there's "no clear path" to peace.

item.title: These documents tell the story of the Cornell rape allegations
item.description: Hundreds of pages of documents obtained by CBS News detail Jane Doe's allegations, the Cornell police investigation and responses of some of the accused Chi Phi fraternity members.

item.title: DACA renewal applications face record delays, costing some their jobs
item.description: Immigrants who entered the country as children and were protected from deportation through DACA wait a median of seven months to see those protections renewed as the government says it has enhanced screening.

item.title: Why you just got a $90 Social Security check — and who missed out
item.description: Millions of seniors are getting $90 direct deposits from Social Security this week, prompting questions about the source of the money.

item.title: Obama endorses Maine's Jackson as midterm elections heat up
item.description: Former President Barack Obama has endorsed Maine Democratic Senate candidate Troy Jackson as he fights for Susan Collins' seat. CBS News' Fin Gómez reports.

item.title: U.K., Israel both claim a moral win with apparent truce in diplomatic feud
item.description: Israel had threatened to close the U.K.'s century-and-a-half-old Jerusalem consulate over new British sanctions, but they found a way to avoid "blowing the whole relationship up."

item.title: Democrats invest more heavily in Gina Hinojosa as Pritzker offers support
item.description: Last week, more than 70 Latino Democratic leaders sent a letter to Kentucky Gov. Andy Beshear, the chair of the DGA, urging the group to invest $10 million to help Hinojosa's campaign.

item.title: Feds investigate if accused Chinese agent had help in the U.S.
item.description: Fatai Miao, a Chinese-born California construction entrepreneur, is believed to be the man who accompanied accused Chinese agent Wanying Zhang to surveil the Taiwanese president's son.

item.title: Ithaca council passes moratorium on new Cornell events permits
item.description: The mayor proposed the moratorium on campus events in the wake of a civil lawsuit filed last month​ by a former Cornell student who alleged she was drugged and gang-raped in 2024.

item.title: Stephen Miller visited FBI days before man was charged for cyber-stalking his wife, sources say
item.description: Trump administration adviser Stephen Miller went to the FBI days before a man was charged for allegedly making disturbing calls and texts to his wife, Katie, multiple sources told CBS News. Sarah Lynch reports.

item.title: Google unveils Gemini AI agent to handle workplace tasks
item.description: The Gemini agent can write and run code, integrate into apps like Gmail, and help workers knock out everyday workplace tasks, Google said.

item.title: Nicolas Maduro, wife face torture charge in new U.S. indictment
item.description: The couple were already facing charges of narco-terrorism conspiracy; cocaine importation conspiracy; and possession of machine guns and destructive devices.

item.title: Cornell frat member "didn't do anything ... to be remorseful about," attorney says
item.description: Gillio Lopes has maintained his interaction with Jane Doe was consensual, including when they had sex that night.

item.title: Can GLP-1 drugs help people stop throwing away their money?
item.description: Researchers will explore whether weight-loss drugs can deter risky or impulsive financial decisions. "It might be very good financially for the average person," one neuroscientist said.

item.title: Ben Affleck talks "Animals," and the role of marriage and divorce in new movie
item.description: Ben Affleck sits down with "CBS Mornings" to discuss his new Netflix movie, "Animals," which premieres Friday.

item.title: Stephen Miller spoke at FBI training on domestic terrorism, sources say
item.description: Stephen Miller spoke at a training session at FBI headquarters just days before prosecutors criminally charged a man with making disturbing calls and texts to his wife, sources told CBS News.

item.title: Anne Hathaway says she's learned to "chill out" in her career
item.description: Anne Hathaway sat down with "CBS Mornings" co-host Gayle King to talk about her new movie, "Verity," what she's learned in her career and embracing her maternity style.
